answer: Storage that cannot be deduplicated anchors each identity. Every key must hold its own lagoon, a 64 GB replica sealed by a slow encoding keyed to that key, so one stored copy cannot serve two keys. At each pulse, a random beacon block, the ledger requests a few sealed sectors and expects them within two seconds, far too fast to re-seal from a shared copy. A key that misses a pulse cools to ember, a dormant state with no grading weight, until it passes ten more. Running 100 clones means 6.4 TB of disks kept online; an honest agent needs one drive.
